title: Scientific Opinion on the substantiation of health claims related to pectins and reduction of post-prandial glycaemic responses (ID 786), maintenance of normal blood cholesterol concentrations (ID 818) and increase in satiety leading to a reduction in energy intake (ID 4692) pursuant to Article 13(1) of Regulation (EC) No 1924/2006
authors: EFSA Panel on Dietetic Products, Nutrition and Allergies (NDA)
funder: European Food Safety Authority, on request from the European Commission (Questions EFSA-Q-2008-1573, EFSA-Q-2008-1605 and EFSA-Q-2010-00645); adopted on 9 July 2010.
result: A cause and effect relationship was established between the consumption of pectins and a reduction of post-prandial glycaemic responses; to bear the claim, at least 10 g of pectins per meal should be consumed, target population adults willing to reduce post-prandial glycaemic responses. A cause and effect relationship was established between the consumption of pectins and maintenance of normal blood cholesterol concentrations; to bear the claim, at least 6 g per day of pectins should be consumed in one or more servings, target population adults. A cause and effect relationship was not established for a sustained increase in satiety leading to a reduction in energy intake; no references were provided from which conclusions could be drawn. The cholesterol assessment rested on Brown et al. (1999): seven pectin studies, 277 subjects, mean 4.7 g per day (2.2 to 9) for a mean 34 days (28 to 42); per gram of pectins per day, total cholesterol changed by -0.07 mmol/L (95% CI -0.117 to -0.022).
